candidates.name: Mycosis fungoides
support_spans: extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions and dry scaly patches, along with the presence of dome-shaped nodules, is consistent with Mycosis fungoides

candidates.name: Sézary syndrome
support_spans: extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
candidates.why: The patient's widespread skin involvement and lymphadenopathy are features that can be seen in Sézary syndrome

candidates.name: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
support_spans: clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism
candidates.why: The presence of a clonal T-cell population and atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism suggests a malignant T-cell process

candidates.name: Mycosis fungoides
support_spans: extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis
positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO
candidates.why: The immunophenotypic profile and histopathologic features are consistent with Mycosis fungoides

candidates.name: Mycosis fungoides
support_spans: biopsy from back nodules showed atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis
immunohistochemical staining showed positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO
candidates.why: The histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings are decisive for the diagnosis of Mycosis fungoides

atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism
